title: Heterogeneous 3+7 order-four boundary across two distinct source banks
body:
## Scope

`recursive-interfaces`, card `persistent-boundary` (scope key `026be4b6e61971d51838`), chooser OS nonce `ba18ac446df7d55ddc50d91395fd9a57`, priority revision 3. Base `e112d71c8d7bb32435debcc54df932593dd8223a`, branch `research/agent-38-persistent-boundary-ba18ac44`. Package: `research/z4-hetero-two-bank-seedba18/`.

Card selection note (pair-collision): the first-choice card `centre-path-sharing` matches already-claimed recent objects (centre-sharing claims in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166 at 12:58 and 13:03 UTC on 2026-10-14), so the second-choice card `persistent-boundary` was taken. This is recorded in `TASK.json`.

**Object.** The one uncovered cell of the pinned [PR 1391](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1391) order-four typed boundary interface: two consecutive root echoes with heterogeneous reader schedules across **two distinct source banks**. Type A has three children reading source octets `[0,1,2]` of bank `X`; type B has seven children reading `[2,1,0,2,1,0,2]` of bank `Y`; one arbitrary dirty output octet and one 24-coordinate arbitrary dirty workspace must both be restored exactly. Predecessors cover 5|5 identical calls on two banks with a midpoint handoff (`research/z4-distinct-source-seed55`) and heterogeneous 3|7 calls on one shared source (`research/z4-heterogeneous-pair-seed3x7`, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1768); neither covers this cell, where the charged 48-ADD source handoff sits at an asymmetric 3|7 boundary. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18932122

## Result

One joint ten-child phase-indexed typed echo with the handoff `W += P^t(Y-X)` after child 2 replaces the two separate calls. Exact maps pass on all 80 basis columns in both directions.

| Execution | ADD | NEG | Primitives | Reads | Prefix row-L1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A then B, separate | 1,552 | 144 | 1,696 | 3,248 | 18 |
| Joint, asymmetric 3-to-7 handoff | 1,408 | 144 | 1,552 | 2,960 | 21 |

Saving: **144 primitives and 288 reads** (8.5%), all costs charged (both forward and literal-inverse child bodies, per-call 48-ADD copy/restore wrappers, the 48-ADD handoff, and both traversals of every phase boundary).

**Boundary law (exact for this alphabet).** The workspace boundary charge has period 4 under the exact recurrence `F_0(t)=A(t)`, `F_(j+1)(s)=min_t F_j(t)+A((s-t-1) mod 4)`, terminal phase 0, with `A = [(0,0),(54,6),(36,12),(54,6)]`: `g(k) = g(k mod 4)`, cross-checked against exhaustive coverage at 64 + 1,024 + 16,384 + 1,048,576 phase paths (k = 3, 5, 7, 10) and for k = 1..16. Consequently `separate(k1,k2) - joint(k1,k2) = 2(g(k1)+g(k2)-g(k1+k2))`, which at total 10 is 144 primitives exactly when both child counts are odd and 0 when both are even. Both sides are confirmed by emitted words: the heterogeneous 3|7 pair realizes the full 144 (invoice identical to the 5|5 case), and a 2|8 pair with the same banks and child family passes both maps with **zero** saving.

## Evidence and reproduction

```sh
python3 -I -B research/z4-hetero-two-bank-seedba18/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/z4-hetero-two-bank-seedba18 --check-only
```

Observed (CPython 3.12, Windows):

```text
PASS_Z4_HETERO_TWO_BANK_3_7 g3=60 g7=60 g10=48 separate=1696 joint=1552 saved=144 reads_saved=288 law=odd_splits_only even28_saved=0 paths=64+1024+16384+1048576 basis=80 controls=6
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
```

`verify.py` re-checks the pinned [PR 1391](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1391)/[PR 1410](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1410) input blobs and the selected-record hash at base, the 12 typed-child identities `Q^(-t)R_b P^t = R_b` and gate counts, recurrence-versus-exhaustive agreement, the exact 5|5 predecessor figures (positive control), the 3|7 and 2|8 exact maps and invoices, and six negative controls (midpoint-instead-of-3|7 switch, wrong handoff phase, mutated A reader, omitted B call, missing terminal Y restoration, missing literal inverse), each rejected by the exact map. `RESULT.json` must match the recomputation byte-for-byte on a second run (it does).

## Limitations and remaining obligations

- Exact only for the declared order-four phase-indexed child alphabet and these fixed reader schedules; not a lower bound for arbitrary ADD/NEG words.
- Output-row reindexing is free in this word model (it is the typed ADD target). Address calculation, physical row routing, source hosting, tape travel, fixed-precision admission, recursive assembly into a selected supplier and analytic transfer are unproved.
- The joint word raises the prefix row-L1 peak from 18 to 21; no precision improvement is claimed.
- No new κ, selected moment, supplier or frontier change. The typed interface remains outside the selected supplier chain.
- The registered package replay (`scripts/research_package.py --package research/z4-hetero-two-bank-seedba18` without `--check-only`) was not launched here; the same `verify.py` was run twice under CPython 3.12 with identical output.

## Credit

Aaron Wang, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no independent human review claimed). Predecessor credit: Cinna Davis (1337isnot1337) for the order-four child family ([PR 1391](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1391)), the same-source persistent boundary ([PR 1410](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1410)), `research/z4-persistent-pair-seed57`, `research/z4-paired-frame-restoration-seed56` and `research/z4-distinct-source-seed55` (typed two-bank 5|5); 1337isnot1337 for `research/z4-heterogeneous-pair-seed3x7` (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1768). The selected-result context is Rohan Arun's https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1094 on Jeremy Kothe's [PR 1087](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1087) construction. All predecessor inputs are pinned byte-for-byte in `inputs/` and `SOURCES.json`.

Workflow note: `make` is not installed on this host, so the selected record's `make frontier1094-verify` cold replay was not run; `scripts/research_baseline.py` printed `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY` for orientation.
